title: Geo-anchored analytics routing with tenant lock & evacuation plan
creator: Amelia Ruiz
description: Implement a geo-anchored routing and tenant-lock mechanism for analytics write and read streams to enforce data residency constraints while providing a controlled evacuation path when region capacity or legal needs change. This ticket covers backend routing rules, shard evacuation choreography, producer backpressure signals, and console controls for operators to schedule or approve cross-region movement.
acceptance_criteria: Write streams for tenants flagged with residency=ENFORCED must route to the configured legal region by default
When a tenant is re-assigned or region is degraded, evacuation coordination moves shards with a staged handoff and records per-shard migration artifacts in the audit log
Routing updates propagate to producers and edge routers within 5 seconds for affected tenants and are visible in the Console routing panel
A test tenant can be moved end-to-end using the new operator flow with no lost records and <=1 minute of consumer catch-up for historical windows
Metrics for staleness, migration duration, in-flight write buffering, and failed-records are emitted to the analytics SLO dashboard
Console exposes a tenant-level residency summary, last-migration timestamp, and active evacuation ticket link
tasks: 1) Design data model for tenant residency metadata and shard affinity rules (DB schema + index)
2) Implement routing middleware that evaluates residency policy and emits sticky route header for downstream stream writers
3) Build shard evacuation controller: plan, pre-copy state, drain writers, handshake with consumer groups, finalize move
4) Add producer client signal protocol for temporary backpressure and fallback routes
5) Instrument metrics and tracing for every step of evacuation (start, pre-copy, drain, commit)
6) Console: operator UI for initiating scheduled evacuation, approve/cancel, and show migration progress
7) Add audit log entries and KMS-tagged artifacts for compliance review
8) End-to-end test harness: synthetic tenant move with verification of zero-data-loss and SLA bounds
9) QA + runbook + postmortem template for live migrations
notes: Background: Customers in EMEA and APAC have requested stronger residency guarantees for usage analytics; upstream effort must prevent accidental cross-border writes while still allowing controlled emergency relocation
Choice: prefer staged evacuation over instantaneous cross-region cutover to minimize write loss and allow legal approvals
Tradeoff: stronger residency constraints will increase tail latency for cross-region fallback; mitigated by local buffering and prefix-KV caching for recent events
Storage considerations: migrations will leverage snapshot-and-incremental-copy to minimize downtime; retention TTLs must be honored in target region
Security: artifacts produced during migration must be encrypted with customer KMS and retained according to retention policy for audits
risks: Edge-case: in-flight writers with long-lived connections may generate partial duplicates during handshake; we must ensure idempotency keys are honored
Operational: large tenants with many shards can take >1hr to evacuate; need an operator-facing priority/parallelism knob
Cost: cross-region data transfer during bulk pre-copy increases egress spend; we need cost-estimate tooling and optional throttles
Legal: some regions require manual sign-off before moving any telemetry data — console must support 'manual-only' mode
dependencies_notes: Relies on INGEST routing feature from ENG-58231 for producer signals
Requires field-level redaction support from ENG-41209 for tenant-specific PII during migration
Coordination with infra team for transient capacity allocation in target region
